about:
We Are More is a locally owned and operated technology integration firm based in Lahaina, Hawaii, on the island of Maui. The company was established in 1984 and has served the Hawaiian islands — including the Big Island, Maui County, Oahu, and Kauai — for decades.

The firm consults, designs, manufactures, installs, and manages a broad range of smart systems for homes, businesses, and marine vessels. Its service portfolio spans acoustical treatment, telecommunications, security, solar, Wi‑Fi and cable networking, voice‑over‑IP, computer networks, network security, home theater, digital signage, lighting, automated locks, shades, blinds, SCADA, and energy monitoring and automation. We Are More holds a Hawaii contractor’s license (C‑35167), a CAGE code (81P78), and is a registered DOE vendor (149246), enabling it to work on city, county, state, and federal projects.

Customers range from residential homeowners seeking smart‑home automation to commercial clients needing integrated security, AV, and IT infrastructure, as well as government agencies at the military, federal, and state levels. The company also serves the marine sector with electronics and automation for vessels.

We Are More emphasizes supplying “the right products for the right reasons” so clients can focus on core activities, and offers financing options to ease project adoption.

Founded in 1913 by Albert Wendling in Charleston, West Virginia, A.F. Wendling's Foodservice began as a fresh meat delivery service. The company remains family-owned and operated, now headquartered in Buckhannon, West Virginia.

Today it operates as West Virginia's largest independent broadline foodservice distributor, supplying more than 9,000 products — fresh meats, seafood, refrigerated and frozen items, and non-food supplies — across West Virginia, Virginia, western Pennsylvania, and surrounding states. The distributor added over 800 square feet of freezer capacity to support expanded service territories and fulfills orders through a direct-delivery model with dedicated customer-service representatives.

The company serves restaurants, institutional kitchens, and other foodservice operators throughout the Mid-Atlantic region. As a member of UniPro Foodservice, it provides access to dozens of exclusive brand lines tailored to diverse menu requirements.

The business was founded to provide reliable fresh meat delivery to local customers and continues to emphasize personalized, customer-focused service — one customer and delivery at a time.

name: West Automotive Products
old_description: Founded in 1983. Our core service is the design, fabrication and delivery of clutch alignment tools that are used in aftermarket clutch kits for thousands of engine types. Using an injection mold process, we currently produce more than 200 unique clutch alignment tools for consumer automobiles, large rigs and agricultural vehicles across North America, in addition to Central American and overseas markets.
about:
West Automotive Products was founded in 1983 in Canby, Oregon, by Don West, a mechanic, entrepreneur, and inventor. West began experimenting with wooden dowels to solve the difficulty of aligning the disc and flywheel during manual transmission clutch replacement, eventually developing a custom plastic injection molding process that became the foundation of the company.

The company designs, fabricates, and delivers clutch alignment tools used in aftermarket clutch kits for thousands of engine types, producing more than 200 unique tools via injection molding. Its Oregon facility handles all design and manufacturing in-house without outsourcing, and also produces drink holders, quick disconnect tools, transmission plugs, seal installers, and timing chain tools. The injection molding process uses 100 percent post-industrial material, and byproducts are re-fabricated to eliminate industrial waste.

West Automotive serves the automotive aftermarket, heavy-duty trucking, and agricultural equipment sectors across North America, Central America, and overseas markets. Its customers include manufacturers of aftermarket clutch kits who rely on the company’s 100 percent fill rates and on-time delivery to meet their own production schedules. The firm works directly with clients’ R&D departments to develop custom alignment tools for new and existing applications.

Don West’s original goal was to bring more precision to clutch replacement, a mission that still drives the company’s quality guarantee — offering full exchange or refund if products do not meet requirements — and its commitment to streamlined, waste-free manufacturing.

about:
West Memphis Steel Corporation operates from West Memphis, Arkansas, where it was founded in 1978. The company has been owned since 1988 by President and CEO Byron P. Besser, who entered the business as the nephew of co‑owner Louis Barg and later acquired the operation.

The firm functions as a full‑line hot‑rolled steel service center, maintaining a large inventory of carbon‑steel products — including plate, sheet, structural shapes, tubing, pipe, and expanded metal — while also providing first‑ and second‑stage processing. Its three Arkansas campuses (Headquarters/Thompson, 7th Street, and Highway 77) house equipment for precision sawing, shearing, brake pressing, flat‑bed laser and plasma cutting, tube laser cutting, robotic welding, drilling/tapping, and assembly and kitting.

West Memphis Steel serves customers across Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee with next‑day truck delivery, and ships nationwide on a weekly schedule. Its client base includes manufacturers and fabricators that require just‑in‑time processed steel, though the company does not publicly list specific industry sectors.

The company states its mission is to improve people’s lives and sustain a family‑style culture where entrepreneurial spirit thrives, aiming to deliver a customer‑service experience that exceeds expectations and enables customers to excel. It emphasizes lean‑manufacturing support through just‑in‑time processing and next‑day delivery to lower operating costs.

name: Western Energy Systems
old_description: Western Energy Systems is a distributor and systems integrator of combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation solutions, including switchgear. Offers fuel gas compressors, battery storage and other power systems, serving utility, commercial and industrial clients.
about:
Western Energy Systems, operating as Northeast-Western Energy Systems USA, LLC (NES-WES), is headquartered in Brea, California. The company traces its roots to 1964 and has accumulated over 50 years of experience in reciprocating engine power applications. In 2023, the business was acquired by the INNIO Group, adding the resources of the Jenbacher product line to its portfolio.

NES-WES functions as a distributor and systems integrator for combined heat and power (CHP) and distributed generation (DG) solutions. The firm engineers and integrates complete systems ranging from 50 kW to 22 MW, incorporating Jenbacher gas engine-generators with balance-of-plant components such as heat recovery, fuel gas handling, emissions control, cooling, chillers, enclosures, switchgear, transformers, and power plant controls. A staff of 200–499 employees handles integration engineering, field project management, commissioning, and ongoing maintenance.

The company serves institutional, commercial, and governmental customers across the energy, utility, industrial, and commercial sectors. Project references include the Bergen County Wastewater Treatment plant, Covidien’s New Haven CHP installation, Mount Joy Wire, a landfill-gas-to-energy facility, High Sierra California Cogeneration, and Techni-Cast industrial cogeneration.

NES-WES emphasizes reducing energy costs, increasing resilience, and lowering carbon footprints for its clients. The 2023 acquisition by INNIO Jenbacher is cited as strengthening its capabilities in the power generation and microgrid markets, while the company’s approach balances innovative solutions with time-tested engineering practices.

name: Western Washington Sheet Metal
old_description: Angela joined the Western Washington Sheet Metal JATC in 2017 after transferring from the SM JATC in Las Vegas, where she had been employed since 2008. Her introduction to the sheet metal industry came through a friend who worked at the JATC and recommended it as a promising career path.
about:
Established in 2008, the Western Washington Sheet Metal Joint Apprenticeship Training Committee (JATC) operates as a non-profit labor-management partnership headquartered in Everett, Washington, with a second campus in DuPont. The committee was formed by the Sheet Metal Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART) Local 66 and the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors' Association (SMACNA) Western Washington to provide standardized apprenticeship training for the region's sheet metal industry. While union apprenticeship in the trade dates back over a century, the modern JATC structure has been in place since 1973.

The JATC delivers tuition-free apprenticeship programs in four core disciplines: sheet metal fabrication and installation, testing adjusting and balancing (TAB), HVAC service, and residential sheet metal. Training combines on-the-job placement with one of 72 signatory contractors—ranging from small shops to large mechanical firms such as MacDonald-Miller, Hermanson Company, and McKinstry—with classroom and lab instruction at the two campuses. The center employs 12 full-time staff, including seven instructors with a combined 210 years of industry experience, and typically enrolls roughly 500 apprentices, graduating about 98 journey-level workers annually.

Graduates enter the commercial construction, HVAC, and building trades sectors, with notable project experience in healthcare facilities, smoke control systems, and energy-efficient heat pump installations recognized by the U.S. Department of Energy. The DuPont campus hosts the SMART Heroes program, which provides a direct entry pathway for active-duty military personnel and veterans. Apprentices earn competitive wages—starting at $70,520 annually with full benefits including retirement, medical, dental, and vision—while incurring zero student debt and receiving credit toward an associate degree.

The JATC's governing board comprises six labor trustees and six management trustees, ensuring curriculum aligns with contractor needs. Instructors bring field expertise from major projects for clients such as Microsoft, SpaceX, Costco, and regional healthcare systems, and hold certifications including WABO welding, TABB, and NEMI/ICB credentials. The program's mission centers on producing a highly skilled, competitive workforce through joint labor-management collaboration.
